title: The Atmosphere
summary: The composition and layers of the atmosphere, the ozone layer, the greenhouse effect and global warming, and how to reduce our impact.

notes.text: The **atmosphere** is the blanket of gases held around the Earth by gravity. It provides the oxygen we breathe and carbon dioxide for photosynthesis, protects us from harmful radiation and meteoroids, and keeps the Earth warm enough for life.

rows: Contains most of the air and water vapour; all weather happens here; temperature decreases with height
Contains the ozone layer; temperature increases with height; jet aircraft fly in the lower part
Coldest layer; meteors burn up here
Very thin air; temperature rises very high; auroras; the International Space Station orbits here

notes.title: Temperature on a mountain
notes.problem: In the troposphere, temperature falls by about 6,5 °C for every kilometre climbed. If it is 25 °C at ground level, what is it 3 km up?

notes.text: **Ozone** (O₃) in the stratosphere absorbs most of the sun's harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**, which causes sunburn, skin cancer and eye damage. Chemicals called **CFCs**, once used in fridges and aerosol sprays, destroyed ozone and created a 'hole' over Antarctica. After CFCs were banned by the **Montreal Protocol** (1987), the ozone layer has slowly begun to recover.

items: Energy from the sun passes through the atmosphere and warms the Earth's surface.
The warm surface gives off heat (infrared radiation).
**Greenhouse gases** (carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour, nitrous oxide) absorb some of this heat and send it back to the surface.
This natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's average temperature at about 15 °C instead of about −18 °C.

notes.caption: The greenhouse effect. Gases in the atmosphere trap some of the heat given off by the warmed surface.

notes.text: Extra greenhouse gases released by human activities trap more heat, causing **global warming**: a rise in the Earth's average temperature.

rows: Carbon dioxide (and fewer trees to absorb it)

notes.text: Effects of **climate change** include more frequent droughts and floods, stronger storms, melting ice and rising sea levels, changing rainfall patterns that affect farming, and loss of species.

items: Use less electricity and switch to renewable energy.
Walk, cycle or use public transport.
Plant indigenous trees; avoid burning rubbish.
Reduce, reuse and recycle; compost food waste to reduce methane from dumps.

notes.title: Why more carbon dioxide warms the Earth
notes.problem: Explain, step by step, how extra carbon dioxide raises the Earth's temperature.
steps: Sunlight passes through the atmosphere and warms the surface.
The warm surface gives off infrared radiation.
Greenhouse gases absorb much of it and send some back down.
More carbon dioxide means more heat is held in the atmosphere.
notes.answer: Extra greenhouse gas traps more of the outgoing heat.

questions.prompt: Name TWO human activities that increase the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): burning fossil fuels; deforestation; cattle farming; landfill/rubbish dumps; fertiliser use

questions.prompt: Give TWO possible effects of global warming on South Africa.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): more droughts; floods/stronger storms; water shortages; crop failure; rising sea levels on the coast; loss of species/biomes
